title: Your 5-Minute Signal: A One-Week Data Audit

sections.title: The Consumption Audit
prompt: List every self-improvement input you consumed last week (podcasts, YouTube, newsletters, books). Be specific — titles, approximate time.
For each item, write one thing you actually did differently because of it. If nothing changed, write 'nothing.'
What's the ratio of consuming to doing in your typical week? What does that number tell you?

sections.title: Your Three-Line Morning Practice
prompt: For the next 7 days, write these three things before opening your phone — what you're worried about today, what you want to accomplish, and one honest sentence about how you're feeling. Set a two-minute timer.
After day 3, read back your entries. What surprised you? What keeps showing up that you didn't expect?
Where in your morning could you realistically do this — what has to happen before it, and what would you be trading it against?

sections.title: Finding the Pattern in Your Own Data
prompt: Look at the last 30 days of your life. When did you feel genuinely good about your work or your day? Write 3-5 specific moments.
What do those moments have in common? Are you building something, analyzing something, connecting with someone, moving your body?
What decision have you been trying to 'figure out' through content consumption that your own daily experience might already be answering?

sections.title: The Belief You're Carrying
prompt: Complete this sentence honestly: 'I consume self-improvement content because I believe ___.' Write the first thing that comes out.
What would you do with your time this week if you genuinely believed you already knew enough to take the next step?
Write one thing your past self — from 6 months ago — would call you out on right now, the way the blog's author was called out by his own journal entry.

cta: Try the three-line practice for just three mornings, then share one thing your own data surfaced that no podcast could have told you.
